symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Asymptotic index along which the panel dimensions and the number of reported event horizons may grow.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Fixed nominal error probability for the simultaneous confidence band.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: A deterministic sequence of tail probabilities used to turn the nonlinear remainder into a coverage-relevant high-probability modulus.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Number of panel units.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of calendar periods.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Index for a panel unit.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Index for a calendar period.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Unit \(i\) first receives the absorbing treatment in period \(G_i\); \(G_i=\infty\) denotes nonadoption within the panel.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: A realized finite adoption date.

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: Set of units adopting in cohort \(g\).

symbols.name: ng
symbols.def: Number of units in cohort \(g\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of post-adoption event horizons reported jointly.

symbols.name: Kn
symbols.def: Set of post-adoption horizons covered simultaneously.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Number of periods elapsed since adoption.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Cohorts observed at event horizon \(k\).

symbols.name: Nk
symbols.def: Number of treated units eligible at event horizon \(k\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Units untreated at the calendar date corresponding to cohort \(g\) and event horizon \(k\).

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: Periods preceding adoption for cohort \(g\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Rank of the untreated conditional-mean matrix.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Matrix of unit loadings with row \(x_i^\top\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Matrix of calendar-time factors with row \(z_t^\top\).

symbols.name: M0
symbols.def: Untreated potential-outcome conditional means, with \(m^0_{it}=x_i^\top z_t\).

symbols.name: Ypot
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(i\) in period \(t\) when its absorbing treatment begins at date \(h\), with \(h=\infty\) denoting no treatment in the panel.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: Mean causal contrast \(\tau_{it}=E[Y_{it}(G_i)-Y_{it}(\infty)]\) for a treated unit-period pair.

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: Idiosyncratic error around the relevant potential-outcome conditional mean.

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.def: Cell-specific heteroskedastic error variance.

symbols.name: sigmarow
symbols.def: Unit-level variance values used by the row-heteroskedastic specialization.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Observed untreated periods used to estimate unit \(i\)'s noise variance.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Number of untreated residual replicates available for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y_{it}=m^0_{it}+\mathbf 1\{t\ge G_i\}\tau_{it}+e_{it}\).

symbols.name: Pseq
symbols.def: \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) is the complete sequence of laws of \(Y\), each conditional on the deterministic arrays \(G,X,Z,\tau\) at index \(n\).

symbols.name: epsVrep
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) variance-replication ratio.

symbols.name: epsSig
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) Choi--Yuan signal ratio.

symbols.name: epsSpec
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) spectral-size ratio.

symbols.name: epsBlock
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) missing-block ratio.

symbols.name: epsLev
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) high-dimensional leverage ratio.

symbols.name: epsRem
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope, fixed before the event-band model class is formed, for the finite-\(n\) anti-concentration-scaled Choi--Yuan remainder bound.

symbols.name: MCYbase
symbols.def: Class of complete Choi--Yuan-regular law arrays \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cy\mbox{-}base\mbox{-}class}\), using common constants and the fixed finite-slice envelopes.
symbols.role: legal complete-array class for the remainder frontier

symbols.name: MCYbaseSlice
symbols.def: The set of \(n\)-th coordinates of complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cy\mbox{-}base\mbox{-}slice}\).

symbols.name: MCY
symbols.def: Subclass of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) whose complete arrays also obey the fixed finite-slice remainder envelope, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cy\mbox{-}event\mbox{-}class}\).

symbols.name: MCYSlice
symbols.def: The set of \(n\)-th coordinates of complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:cy\mbox{-}event\mbox{-}slice}\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: Union of all observed treated, donor, and pre-treatment cells used by the eligible Choi--Yuan blocks.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Observed untreated cells whose leave-one-cell-out residual squares estimate the unit-specific variances.

symbols.name: Qplus
symbols.def: Union of every primitive influence cell and every cell used to train the variance estimator.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: One unit-period cell used by at least one event-horizon expansion.

symbols.name: xbar
symbols.def: Mean unit loading in cohort \(g\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Left-factor Gram matrix for the donor rows in block \((g,k)\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Right-factor Gram matrix over the pre-adoption periods for cohort \(g\).

symbols.name: Nb
symbols.def: Number of rows in the Choi--Yuan block for cohort \(g\) and horizon \(k\).

symbols.name: Tb
symbols.def: Number of columns in the Choi--Yuan block containing the pre-adoption periods and target calendar period.

symbols.name: Ublock
symbols.def: Left singular-vector matrix in a compact singular-value decomposition of the restriction of \(M^0\) to rows \(I_g\cup J_{gk}\) and columns \(S_g\cup\{g+k\}\).

symbols.name: Vblock
symbols.def: Right singular-vector matrix in the same compact block singular-value decomposition.

symbols.name: psi
symbols.def: Smallest nonzero singular value of the untreated mean in block \(g,k\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: Spectral condition number of the untreated mean in block \(g,k\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: Choi--Yuan incoherence index for block \(g,k\).

symbols.name: Ce
symbols.def: Uniform sub-Gaussian norm multiplier.

symbols.name: sigmalo
symbols.def: Uniform lower bound for cell standard deviations.

symbols.name: sigmahi
symbols.def: Uniform upper bound for cell standard deviations.

symbols.name: mubar
symbols.def: Uniform upper bound for block incoherence.

symbols.name: cA
symbols.def: Lower donor-Gram eigenvalue constant.

symbols.name: CA
symbols.def: Upper donor-Gram eigenvalue constant.

symbols.name: cB
symbols.def: Lower pre-period-Gram eigenvalue constant.

symbols.name: CB
symbols.def: Upper pre-period-Gram eigenvalue constant.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: \(c_{k,(u,v)}=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_g,\,v=g+k\}}{n_g}-\mathbf 1\{u\in J_{gk},\,v=g+k\}\bar x_g^\top A_{gk}^{-1}x_u-\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_g,\,v\in S_g\}}{n_g}z_{g+k}^\top B_g^{-1}z_v\right]\).

symbols.name: Qshared
symbols.def: Primitive cells whose exact aggregated influence coefficients are nonzero at both horizons \(k\) and \(k'\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_{uv}^2\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Marginal standard deviation of the linear event-horizon influence sum.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Diagonal matrix of event-horizon standard deviations.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Coefficient of the standardized primitive error \(e_{uv}/\sigma_{uv}\) in horizon \(k\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Largest standardized contribution of one primitive panel cell to the event curve.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: Correlation matrix of the standardized event-curve influence sum.

symbols.name: Zgauss
symbols.def: Gaussian vector with the full staircase correlation matrix.

symbols.name: hatM
symbols.def: The Choi--Yuan nuclear-norm block estimator with their debiasing map, applied separately to every eligible block \((g,k)\).

symbols.name: hattau
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k})\).

symbols.name: thet
symbols.def: \(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}=N_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k}\).

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})-\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\).

symbols.name: hatc
symbols.def: Plug-in version of \(c\) formed from the Choi--Yuan debiased block loading and factor estimates and the observed cohort sizes.

symbols.name: hate
symbols.def: For each \(q=(i,t)\in\mathcal V_n\), refit the Choi--Yuan rank-\(r\) completion and debiasing map on the observed untreated staircase with cell \(q\) deleted, and set \(\widehat e_{it}=Y_{it}-\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-q)}\).

symbols.name: hatsigmarow
symbols.def: Residual-square estimator of unit \(i\)'s time-invariant noise variance.

symbols.name: hatOmega
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}\widehat c_{kq}\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u^2\).

symbols.name: hats
symbols.def: Diagonal studentization extracted from the heteroskedastic plug-in covariance.

symbols.name: hatSigma
symbols.def: Studentized plug-in correlation matrix retaining all shared-cell products.

symbols.name: xi
symbols.def: Multipliers independent of the observed panel.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Conditional multiplier analogue of the supremum of the studentized event-curve error.

symbols.name: calpha
symbols.def: Conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of the Gaussian-multiplier maximum.

symbols.name: Band
symbols.def: One studentized multiplier band indexed by all eligible event horizons.

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: Positive part of the simultaneous undercoverage of the uninflated studentized multiplier band under one legal triangular-array law.

symbols.name: RCY
symbols.def: Set \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}=\frac{\bar\sigma^2\kappa_{gk}^5\mu_{gk}r}{\psi_{gk}}\frac{\max\{N_{gk}\log N_{gk},T_g\log T_g\}}{\min\{N_{gk},T_g\}}+\bar\sigma\kappa_{gk}^4\mu_{gk}^2r^2\frac{\max\{\sqrt{N_{gk}\log N_{gk}},\sqrt{T_g\log T_g}\}}{\min\{N_{gk}^{3/2},T_g^{3/2}\}}+\bar\sigma n_g\mu_{gk}^2r^2\kappa_{gk}^3\frac{\max\{\sqrt{N_{gk}\log N_{gk}},\sqrt{T_g\log T_g}\}}{N_{gk}\min\{N_{gk},T_g\}}\).

symbols.name: DeltaCY
symbols.def: Cohort-share aggregation of the exact published block remainder bounds on the studentized event scale.

symbols.name: deltaP
symbols.def: Upper \(1-\eta_n\) quantile of the exact standardized nonlinear remainder under one law.

symbols.name: DeltaStar
symbols.def: Worst-law upper \(1-\eta_n\) quantile of the exact standardized nonlinear remainder over the explicitly defined \(n\)-th slice of the baseline complete-array class.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: A deterministic positive sequence formed only from the published Choi--Yuan block ratios, cohort shares, and marginal studentization scales.

symbols.name: DeltaSharp
symbols.def: Primitive block-ratio expression to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:attainable\mbox{-}remainder\mbox{-}frontier}\) and shown uniformly equivalent to \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\).

symbols.name: underorder
symbols.def: Strict asymptotic order used to quantify a proposed primitive envelope that understates the attainable uniform remainder scale.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(\{e_{it}:(i,t)\in\mathcal Q_n^+\}\) are mutually independent under \(P_n\).

standard.name: Independent cell noise in structured matrix completion

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(\|e_{it}\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\sigma_{it}\) for every \((i,t)\in\mathcal Q_n^+\), with the same \(C_e\).

For every \(n\), \(0<\underline\sigma\le\min_{(i,t)\in\mathcal Q_n^+}\sigma_{it}\le\max_{(i,t)\in\mathcal Q_n^+}\sigma_{it}\le\bar\sigma<\infty\), with the same \(\underline\sigma\) and \(\bar\sigma\).
For every \(n\), \(\sigma_{it}^2=\sigma_i^2\) for every \(i\le N\) and \(t\le T\).

standard.name: Unit-specific heteroskedasticity for a feasible low-rank group-average CLT

novel.justification: The envelope is satisfied when every unit retains an untreated history that grows faster than \(\log(2N)\log^4(2K)\). Long administrative and policy panels with adoption bounded away from the first sample periods provide this replication while allowing the reported horizon set to grow.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(\max_{g\in E_k,k\in\mathcal K_n}\mu_{gk}\le\bar\mu\), with the same \(\bar\mu\).

standard.name: Uniform version of the Choi--Yuan signal-to-noise ratio
Uniform version of the Choi--Yuan spectral dimension ratio
Uniform version of the Choi--Yuan missing-block ratio

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(c_A|J_{gk}|I_r\preceq A_{gk}\preceq C_A|J_{gk}|I_r\) for all \(g\in E_k\) and \(k\in\mathcal K_n\), with the same \(c_A,C_A\).
For every \(n\), \(c_B|S_g|I_r\preceq B_g\preceq C_B|S_g|I_r\) for all \(g\in E_k\) and \(k\in\mathcal K_n\), with the same \(c_B,C_B\).

novel.justification: This is a primitive uniformization of the published block ratios rather than a condition on an estimated remainder. It is satisfied by balanced strong-factor panels with fixed rank, bounded condition numbers, cohort blocks of vanishing panel share, and polynomially growing horizon sets, a configuration approximated by long staggered state-policy panels after restricting to eligible cohorts.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ctr}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{subG}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{var}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rowvar}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{vrep}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{vrep}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rank}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{inc}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{sig}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{sig}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{spec}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{spec}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{block}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{block}})\wedge\mathsf A_A((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_B((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{nd}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{lev}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{lev}})\}\). Every member property holds at each finite \(n\) with the single constants \(C_e,\underline\sigma,\bar\sigma,\bar\mu,c_A,C_A,c_B,C_B\) and the fixed envelopes displayed in the symbol table.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\)
definitions.construction: For each finite \(n\), define \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}=\{P_n: \exists (P_j)_{j\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\text{ whose }n\text{-th coordinate is }P_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rem}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{rem}})\}\). Equivalently, every finite slice obeys \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{rem}}\) for the one fixed vanishing envelope \(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{rem}}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\)
definitions.construction: For each finite \(n\), define \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}=\{P_n: \exists (P_j)_{j\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\text{ whose }n\text{-th coordinate is }P_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{event}}\)
definitions.construction: For every \(k\in\mathcal K_n\), apply the exact Choi--Yuan debiasing map to each eligible block \((g,k)\), then compute \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k})\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak C_n\)
definitions.construction: Map every eligible block to its exact Proposition A.4 donor-row and treated-preperiod coefficients, add the observed treated-cell coefficient, aggregate by \(n_g/N_k\), and return the array \(c=(c_{kq})\) defined in the symbol table.

definitions.name: \(\widehat\Omega_n\)
definitions.construction: On the variance-training set \(\mathcal V_n\), compute each untreated residual \(\widehat e_{it}\) from the rank-\(r\) Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing fit with cell \((i,t)\) deleted, and set \(\widehat\sigma_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}\widehat e_{it}^2\). Estimate the exact influence coefficients \(\widehat c_{kq}\), and set \(\widehat\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}\widehat c_{kq}\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u^2\) for all \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\); no variance-training cell outside \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\) enters this influence sum.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n\)
definitions.construction: For \(q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\), draw \(\xi_q\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\), compute \(W_n^\xi=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u\xi_q/\widehat s_k|\), take its conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile \(c_{1-\alpha,n}\), and report \(\mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\).

definitions.name: \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\)
definitions.construction: After forming the finite slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), for \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) and \(0<\eta_n<1/2\), set \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)=\inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\)
definitions.construction: For every vanishing sequence \(\eta=(\eta_n)\) and each finite \(n\), set \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)=\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\), where \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) is the previously defined \(n\)-th slice of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).

definitions.name: \(\triangleleft\)
definitions.construction: For a candidate primitive envelope \(\beta_n(K)\) and the frontier output \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), define \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) if and only if \(\beta_n(K)/\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\to0\).

definitions.name: \(\Gamma_n(P_n)\)
definitions.construction: Set \(\Gamma_n(P_n)=\bigl[(1-\alpha)-P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}\bigr]_+\), using the uninflated conditional multiplier critical value.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\)
definitions.construction: Set \(N=8\), \(T=3\), \(r=1\), \(K=2\), \(G_i=2\) for \(i=1,\ldots,4\), and \(G_i=\infty\) for \(i=5,\ldots,8\). Set \(x_i=1\), \(z_t=1\), and \(\sigma_{it}^2=1\) for every cell. Thus \(I_2=\{1,2,3,4\}\), \(J_{2,0}=J_{2,1}=\{5,6,7,8\}\), \(S_2=\{1\}\), and \(N_0=N_1=4\). Apply the displayed coefficient formula for \(c_{kq}\) at \(k=0,1\).

definitions.name: second-order staircase alignment handle
definitions.construction: Expand the Choi--Yuan block KKT equations and debiasing map exactly to second order on balanced rank-one complete triangular arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), retain signed singular-space perturbations before applying norm inequalities, align their signs across nested adoption blocks, and optimize the resulting per-law quantiles over the explicitly defined finite slices to derive a primitive expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) equivalent to \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\).

definitions.name: RTC-law event-curve protocol
definitions.construction: On the 1977--2014 right-to-carry panel, retain the 44 states with at least eight pre-adoption observations, define \(G_i\) by the law's first effective year, apply \(\mathcal C_n\) to the eligible post-adoption subcurve \(k=0,\ldots,10\), retain \(k=-20,\ldots,-1\) as an observed pre-fit diagnostic outside the band theorem, and residualize the optional unit and calendar effects before block completion.

statements.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), the eligible-cohort estimator satisfies \[D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})=\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,\qquad \|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)).\] The coefficients are obtained by aggregating the exact Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 block coefficients with eligible-unit weights \(n_g/N_k\) before any covariance calculation.
statements.justification: This is the missing bridge from scalar block debiasing to one growing adoption-aligned event process.
statements.gap: Choi and Yuan, Proposition A.4 and their staggered-adoption theorem, give block or scalar expansions but do not aggregate an increasing number of event horizons uniformly.
statements.consumer: It supplies the vector score needed to attach whole-curve uncertainty to the Ben-Michael--Feller right-to-carry event plot.

statements.statement: For all \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\), mutual independence and centeredness on \(\mathcal Q_n^+\) give the algebraic identity \[\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}\!\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{k'q}e_q\right)=\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2.\] Terms outside \(\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\) vanish by definition, and \(\Omega_{kk'}\ne0\) if and only if the displayed signed shared-cell sum is nonzero; individual products may cancel. Studentization is the identity \(\Sigma_n=D_n^{-1}\Omega_nD_n^{-1}\).
statements.justification: This bookkeeping lemma fixes the signed shared-cell covariance that the feasible rate theorem and multiplier law must estimate.
statements.gap: The identity is not an independent novelty claim; it records the covariance implied by the exact aggregated Choi--Yuan coefficients.
statements.consumer: It prevents implementations from treating overlapping donor and pre-treatment cells as independent blocks.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\), the untreated mean has rank one, \(\mu_{2,0}=\mu_{2,1}=1\), \(A_{2,0}=A_{2,1}=4\), and \(B_2=1\). At each horizon, the four treated target cells have coefficient \(1/4\), the four donor target cells have coefficient \(-1/4\), and the four treated pre-period cells shared by both horizons have coefficient \(-1/4\). Therefore each marginal variance is \(12(1/4)^2=3/4\), each shared-cell covariance product is \((-1/4)(-1/4)=1/16\), the off-diagonal covariance is \(4/16=1/4\), and the correlation is \((1/4)/(3/4)=1/3\). This explicitly satisfies the noncancellation condition in \(\mathrm{lem:staircase\mbox{-}covariance}\).
statements.justification: The fully enumerated finite panel verifies the coefficient normalization and exhibits a nonzero signed shared-cell sum without appealing to an unnamed procedure.
statements.gap: No located low-rank staggered-adoption inference result displays this exact two-horizon coefficient calculation; the proposition is an algebraic witness, not a claim that a published method imposes block independence.
statements.consumer: The twelve-cell calculation is a deterministic unit test for implementations of the full RTC-law event covariance.

statements.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), use leave-one-cell-out residuals only on \(\mathcal V_n\), while keeping the covariance sum on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). The resulting unit-heteroskedastic plug-in estimator satisfies \[\max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|/(s_ks_{k'})=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2}),\qquad \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat s_k/s_k-1|=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-1}).\] In particular, \(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) while retaining every shared treated-, donor-, and pre-treatment-cell product.
statements.justification: The multiplier law is usable only if its entire growing covariance matrix, not only each diagonal entry, is estimable under bounded unit heteroskedasticity.
statements.gap: The accessible Choi--Yuan article points to Supplement G.2 but does not substantiate a horizon-uniform covariance theorem; Choi--Kwon--Liao's Feasible CLT displays unitwise residual variance only for a fixed group-average functional, and Ben-Michael--Feller leave staggered heteroskedastic inference as a last-mile task.
statements.consumer: This gives the feasible covariance input for one studentized whole-curve critical value in a state-policy panel.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), with \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) the \(n\)-th slice of the complete-array class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), \[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\left(\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z\right)-P_n\left(\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|\le z\right)\right|\to0,\quad Z_n\sim N(0,\Sigma_n),\] and the conditional law of \(W_n^\xi\) has the same limit uniformly over this slice. Therefore \[\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}}P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}\to1-\alpha.\] The complete class includes arrays with \(K_n\to\infty\) and nonzero staircase off-diagonals, so this strictly goes beyond scalar Choi--Yuan inference.
statements.justification: This is the headline whole-path coverage result for an identified event curve under structured MNAR completion.
statements.gap: Choi--Yuan establish scalar or blockwise normality; Yan--Wainwright give entrywise intervals; Xia--Yan--Wainwright give heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals; and Callaway--Sant'Anna give simultaneous paths under parallel trends. None supplies the joint growing-\(K_n\) law, shared-cell covariance estimation, and simultaneous Choi--Yuan multiplier band.
statements.consumer: The right-to-carry analysis can replace pointwise visual uncertainty with one honest band over all reported exposure durations.

statements.statement: When \(K=1\) and the eligible set contains one target block, \(c_{0q}\) and \(\Omega_{00}\) reduce to the Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 influence coefficients and their heteroskedastic scalar influence variance, while \(\widehat\Omega_{00}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,0}\) reduce to the Choi--Kwon--Liao-style unit-residual plug-in variance and the ordinary studentized scalar interval.
statements.justification: The required reduction rules out an event-time construction that changes the published scalar target or coefficients.
statements.gap: This is a fidelity check against Choi--Yuan rather than an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Existing scalar implementations obtain the new procedure by setting the horizon set to one element.

statements.statement: Using the second-order staircase alignment handle, derive a primitive block-ratio expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that \[c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\] for every vanishing tail sequence \(\eta_n\), where \(\Delta_n^*\) is optimized over the explicitly defined slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\). Establish the coverage frontier in this finite-slice experiment: \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) must imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\); conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) and \(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero, construct one complete staggered low-rank triangular array \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) satisfying \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), and \(\liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0\). The derivation must first test whether the balanced strong-factor rank-one second-order remainder is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so, \(\Delta^{\dagger}\) must use the smaller attained scale.
statements.justification: The honest open content is necessity: published norm bounds can be sufficient yet unattainable by any legal low-rank staircase panel.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Koike give nearly sharp generic vector-sum arrays, but those arrays need not arise from the Choi--Yuan debiasing map; no source establishes an attainable panel-specific converse.
statements.consumer: A resolved frontier tells empirical researchers exactly how far the event horizon may grow without ad hoc band inflation and prevents overclaiming a coarse perturbation bound as sharp.

sampling_model.design: Deterministic absorbing staggered adoption with the untreated cells missing by a nested staircase after each unit's adoption date.
sampling_model.units: A complete triangular array of deterministic low-rank mean panels with common regularity constants, fixed vanishing finite-slice rate envelopes, and jointly independent centered sub-Gaussian errors on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\). Variances are time-invariant within units but may differ across units, and both \(N_n\) and \(T_n\) may grow.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal effect is added after \(G_i\); the target averages eligible treated units with unit-share rather than equal-cohort weights.
sampling_model.overlap: Every eligible cohort-horizon block has donor-row and pre-period Gram eigenvalues bounded uniformly away from zero after size normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Exact Choi--Yuan blockwise nuclear-norm estimation and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals on \(\mathcal V_n\), unit-level residual variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and a Gaussian multiplier summed only over \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\).

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),\quad \mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: With appropriate debiasing, the proposed estimate is asymptotically normal even with fairly weak signals.
Event-time aggregation crosses calendar times and right factors, so its normal approximation and variance may differ from calendar-time inference.
The multiplier bootstrap yields asymptotically valid simultaneous inference for staggered group-time treatment effects under conditional parallel trends.
The data-driven intervals estimate each missing panel entry and match an instance-wise Bayesian Cramer--Rao lower bound.
The preprint gives heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for individual effects and general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under staggered adoption.
The Gaussian and bootstrap approximation bounds are sharp in dimension and envelope for generic bounded high-dimensional vector sums.
Gaussian anti-concentration permits honest multiplier confidence bands without requiring a fixed extreme-value limit.

tldr: Choi--Yuan make weak-signal inference possible for structured MNAR blocks, but adoption-aligned event-time aggregation reuses donor and pre-treatment cells across calendar columns, so scalar variances do not determine a whole-path band. The project fixes the eligible-cohort unit-share event estimand, aggregates the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients into a growing-dimensional influence representation, records the resulting staircase covariance as supporting algebra, proves a feasible leave-one-cell-out covariance-rate theorem, and obtains an honest studentized Gaussian-multiplier band. Noise conditions cover the joint domain of influence and variance-training cells, while covariance and multiplier sums remain restricted to influence cells. An explicit finite rank-one two-horizon witness verifies normalization and produces correlation \(1/3\) from four shared cells. The exact attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remains the first-class open question because the balanced strong-factor kill test indicates that the published norm envelope may be logarithmically loose.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR results provide entrywise, scalar, or fixed block inference. Published staggered DiD results provide simultaneous event paths under parallel trends. Neither literature derives a growing adoption-aligned Choi--Yuan influence array, its shared-cell covariance, and a primitive feasible unit-heteroskedastic multiplier law.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a studentized event-curve theorem whose summands are primitive panel cells rather than cohorts, because one cell can enter several Choi--Yuan blocks and create persistent off-diagonal covariance.
project_justification.fill: The exact block coefficients are aggregated into one event-by-cell map, the Choi--Yuan perturbation ratios are bounded at each finite \(n\) by fixed vanishing envelopes over a complete-array class, and each finite optimization uses an explicitly induced slice. Residual-square training is confined to \(\mathcal V_n\), all noise conditions hold on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\), and the feasible covariance and multiplier sums remain on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). Gaussian approximation plus anti-concentration then yields honest whole-curve coverage. The open necessity node asks for the smaller attained remainder scale rather than declaring the coarse sufficient envelope sharp.

related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, the main-text Noise Assumption, Proposition A.4, the staggered-adoption theorem, variance-estimation corollary, and Supplement G.2, supply the exact donor-row and treated-preperiod linear terms and primitive perturbation ratios. Their main-text residual variance is pooled, and the stated heteroskedastic extension remains scalar or blockwise; no cited result supplies a horizon-uniform unitwise variance-replication rate, so that rate is imposed here as a novel complete-array condition. Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, Sections 2--4, articulate the calendar-time versus event-time boundary, request staggered heteroskedastic inference, and document the 44-state right-to-carry application. Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, Theorem 3, Corollary 3, and Algorithm 1, provide the closest cohort-time aggregation and simultaneous multiplier-band writing template, but their score arises from conditional parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Main Results 1--2, provide Gaussian and multiplier approximation for correlated coordinate maxima, and their confidence-band paper, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands}, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, identifies the anti-concentration scale at which a uniform nonlinear remainder affects coverage. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Koike, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKoike2023NearlyOptimal}, Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 2.1, sharpen generic approximation bounds and lower arrays, but their arrays are not constrained by one low-rank factorization and a nested adoption staircase. Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, Theorems 1--2 and Discussion, deliver instance-optimal entrywise intervals under staggered missingness, not an eligible unit-share event curve or its simultaneous law. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, the abstract and introduction, pages 5--6, equations (2)--(4), Sections 3.1--3.3, and page 20, give heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for individual effects and general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under a low-rank staggered staircase. Their result informs the scalar low-rank comparison; the missing object here is the joint growing-\(K_n\) law, estimation of covariance created by reused influence cells, and one simultaneous multiplier band for the Choi--Yuan eligible event curve. Xia and Yuan, \cite{XiaYuan2021LinearForms}, Theorem 1 and its alignment examples, show that low-rank linear-form variance depends on singular-space alignment, which explains why event-time aggregation cannot discard calendar-factor geometry. Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, the Feasible CLT and its displayed \(\widehat\sigma_i^2\) residual estimator, substantiate unit-specific heteroskedasticity for a fixed group-average functional; they do not supply the novel \(K_n\)-uniform replication envelope or a growing event path. Their rank-robust sequel, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2026Rank}, Introduction and feasible block-average theorem, identifies a Tikhonov-type bias from rank over-specification, motivating the approximate-rank sensitivity seed without subsuming the exact-rank band kernel. Athey et al., \cite{AtheyEtAl2021MatrixCompletion}, cross-validation paragraph and Conclusions, establish the causal-panel nuclear-norm and random-cell validation baseline but not debiased simultaneous inference. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein, \cite{BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022StaggeredSC}, linear-factor error theorem and Discussion, separate individual and pooled imbalance for staggered synthetic controls, informing the alternative combine-before-apply seed. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu, \cite{ChernozhukovWuthrichZhu2021Conformal}, exact-validity theorem and weak-dependence theory, give symmetry-based counterfactual inference; their route requires exchangeability or stationarity not supplied by the Choi--Yuan class.
technical_internal_limitation: The nominal Choi--Yuan envelope is obtained after several operator- and maximum-norm inequalities. In the balanced strong-factor rank-one calculation, the exact second-order terms are smaller by at least a logarithmic factor than this envelope under every symmetric split checked. This diagnostic prevents presenting \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log K}\to0\) as necessary. It does not affect its role as a sufficient primitive condition for the band theorem.
honest_scope: The settled target is conditional-mean event-time inference under exact low rank and independent unit-heteroskedastic cell noise on the full analysis domain \(\mathcal Q_n^+\). Serially dependent errors, approximate low rank, data-selected rank and penalties, and combine-before-apply efficiency are separate kernels. The staircase covariance formula is a supporting identity, while the substantive results are the uniform influence representation, feasible growing covariance rate, and joint multiplier approximation. The fixed-horizon reduction recovers the Choi--Yuan scalar result. The finite \(1/3\)-correlation witness is an algebraic sanity reduction, not an attribution of block independence to any published estimator. The model is a class of complete triangular arrays with common constants and fixed vanishing rate envelopes; every finite optimization uses its explicitly induced \(n\)-th slice. The exact attainable remainder modulus and the ordered under-envelope counterarray remain open in \(\mathrm{oeq:attainable-remainder-frontier}\); no sharpness claim is made for the coarse published envelope.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem is Choi--Yuan's Proposition A.4 and staggered scalar CLT; Xia--Yan--Wainwright already cover heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic inference for general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under a low-rank staggered staircase; and the closest whole-path template is Callaway--Sant'Anna's multiplier band. The precise unoccupied intersection is a growing event-by-cell influence array obtained from the exact Choi--Yuan block coefficients, a feasible covariance estimator that retains signed products over reused primitive cells, and a joint studentized multiplier approximation over growing horizons. The covariance product formula is supporting algebra rather than a separate theorem. The explicit rank-one \(1/3\)-correlation witness verifies normalization and noncancellation. Sharpness of the published remainder envelope is not claimed: it is isolated as an attainable-modulus open question after the early rank-one kill test exposed likely logarithmic slack.
message: Re-rooted the proposal at the uniform vector influence representation, feasible growing covariance rate, and multiplier-band theorem. The shared-cell covariance identity is now a supporting lemma; influence cells, variance-training cells, and their joint noise domain are separated; and the Xia--Yan--Wainwright comparison now acknowledges general scalar weighted bilinear confidence intervals while isolating the missing growing-dimensional joint law.
